- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.27) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +5% above peak or adjust downward if sentiment drops.  
- If sentiment is high (≥0.77) and price is trending up, model may overfit momentum; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% if sentiment stabilizes.  
- If true outcome is significantly below forecast (e.g., >5% gap), check if sentiment was high recently — if so, apply mean reversion: subtract 1–2% per day until sentiment drops.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in the period; apply a 1–2% downward bias for first 5–7 days if sentiment is neutral or declining.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 values, model tends to underestimate; add 2–4% to forecast for next 3–5 days.
